model.notes: torque printed '1.2 N.m' (implausible) -> read as 1.2 kg.cm; 13-line encoder 3.3-5 V; mass not published (A 50 g)

source.cad_c1_pay300: checks/fit_check_v2.json scout_v2_c1 (300 g payload at x=-73.9 mm)

sim_disagreement.note: sim (v1 fallback, 0.80 kg + 0.3 kg) stalls at 0.11 Nm/wheel; quasi-static model needs 0.057-0.066 Nm with the heavier CAD mass. Factor ~1.7-2 unexplained (MuJoCo soft contact / rolling-friction torque / velocity-PID saturation). Resolve with the free bench test T1 before buying motors.

motor_review.spin_verdict: Traction allows it (L/B = 0.645 < 1). Kinematics: wheels must run 1.7-1.9x the geometric speed (sim), i.e. 32-37 wheel rpm -- easy. Torque: 0.047 (carpet) - 0.055 (hard, mu 0.8) N m per wheel vs 0.0785 N m printed stall of TT-class motors -> SF 1.1-1.5 at the motor's own rated voltage. Achievable ONLY with gyro-closed-loop yaw-rate control (sim open-loop: 0.45-0.65 rad/s; closed-loop gyro: 1.0 rad/s). Requirement change proposed: REQ-SCOUT-001 angular target 1 rad/s measured by the IMU, with Nav2 max_vel_theta 0.8 rad/s for margin.

pi5_8gb_active_cooler.src: D/M cnx-software wall meter: idle 3.0 W headless, stress -c 4 8.8 W (https://www.cnx-software.com/2023/11/05/raspberry-pi-5-review-raspberry-pi-os-bookworm-benchmarks-power-consumption/); typ A: SLAM+Nav2+detector ~2-3 cores busy; peak A: 8.8 W + 1.2 W USB/GPU margin

camera_module_3.src: A: no official power figure published; IMX708 streaming estimate, bound 0.3-1.0 W

lidar_c1.src: D 5 V x 230 mA operating (https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/RPLIDAR_C1); start-up not published -> A 300 mA

esp32_devkit_wifi_off.src: A from ESP32 datasheet modem-sleep 20-68 mA @240 MHz + LDO/USB-UART losses (https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32_datasheet_en.pdf)

encoders_x4.src: A ~10 mA each at 5 V (hall sensor + pull-ups); not in the Hiwonder listing

hcsr04_imu_mdd3a_logic.src: D HC-SR04 15 mA @5 V (https://cdn.sparkfun.com/datasheets/Sensors/Proximity/HCSR04.pdf); D MPU-6050 3.9 mA; A MDD3A logic

battery.why_label_implausible: 634 Wh/L at pack level; good cylindrical cells alone reach ~600-700 Wh/L and a 15 mm-thick pack cannot hold 18650s, so these are pouch cells + BMS + wrap: expect ~230-520 Wh/L -> 12-27.5 Wh (A)

brownout.verdict: Pi 5 V rail survives a 4-motor stall even at R_pack 0.25 ohm and a 9.6 V pack (the buck needs only ~5.9 V in). The real brown-out mechanism is the pack's BMS over-current trip (rating UNKNOWN): if it trips below the burst current the whole robot, Pi included, loses power. Read the pack/BMS markings; add a firmware stall-current limit (back-EMF model from encoder speed).

pololu_d36v50f5.vin: 5.5-50 V; dropout ~0.83 V @1 A, ~0.92 V @3 A, ~1.0 V @5 A (graph) -> regulates down to ~6 V in; pack floor 9.0 V leaves >= 3 V headroom
pololu_d36v50f5.iout: ~8.0 A continuous at 9-18 V in, still air (graph); 5.5 A at 36 V
pololu_d36v50f5.protection: reverse input to 40 V, OCP, short, thermal, soft-start, PG output, EN pin (D)
pololu_d36v50f5.weak_point: fixed 5.0 V: REQ-SCOUT-012 lower limit 5.0 V is not guaranteed after tolerance and lead drop

xl4015_generic.verdict: DON'T BUY as the Pi supply
xl4015_generic.why: listing rates ~3.5 A sustained without extra cooling (round-1 source manuals.plus B078JTR9GM) < 5 A Pi spec; no reverse protection, no PG; trim pot drifts with vibration; 51 x 26 x 14 mm. Only advantage: can be trimmed to 5.15 V.

ubec_5A_generic.why: no datasheet with output tolerance, ripple or dropout found; hobby UBECs are specified for servo loads, not for a 5.0-5.25 V window

pi_supply.REQ_SCOUT_012: 5.0-5.25 V NOT guaranteed by a fixed 5.0 V +/-4 % buck (tolerance as read in round 1 -- re-verify) -> propose: '>= 4.9 V at the header under load and vcgencmd get_throttled == 0x0 over 30 min', or verify the delivered unit reads >= 5.0 V at 3 A before installing
pi_supply.usb_current: Without USB-PD the Pi 5 limits downstream USB to 600 mA total; with a 5 A-capable supply it gives 1.6 A (https://github.com/raspberrypi/documentation/blob/master/documentation/asciidoc/computers/raspberry-pi/power-supplies.adoc). GPIO back-powering cannot negotiate PD, so set usb_max_current_enable=1 in config.txt (and PSU_MAX_CURRENT=5000 in the EEPROM, round-1 source https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/685-app-notes-guides-whitepapers/documents/RP-009856-WP-1-USB%20Power%20delivery%20on%20Raspberry%20Pi%205.pdf). USB load: LiDAR 230-300 mA (+ ESP32 ~100-250 mA if powered over USB) = 0.33-0.55 A -> fits even 600 mA, but start-up surges make it marginal: set the flag.
pi_supply.wiring: buck VOUT -> header pins 2 and 4, GND -> pins 6 and 14; 20 AWG, <= 15 cm; keyed connector; GPIO 5 V bypasses the Pi's input protection -> verify polarity with the multimeter, never hot-plug the 5 V lead
pi_supply.heat: buck loss 0.72 W typical, 0.86 W peak, 1.32 W at 5 A -- fine for a 25 mm board in the lower deck; keep >= 5 mm air gap to the battery

motor_rail.decision: NO separate motor buck. MDD3A (4-16 V) straight on the pack, PWM duty capped in firmware to V_cap / V_batt with V_cap = 8.4 V (Hiwonder, rated 3-12 V) or 7.4 V (FIT0450, max 7.5 V); V_batt from the ESP32 ADC.
motor_rail.why_no_buck: a 5 A motor buck would current-limit exactly when torque is needed (climb 1.2-2.4 A/channel, 4-motor stall 6-7 A) and adds a part; the CAD's D36V28F-class motor buck (2.8 A family) is far too small and also overlaps buck_5v in fit_check_v2.json
motor_rail.pwm_heating: at 20 kHz the motor's electrical time constant (L/R ~0.1-0.5 ms, A: 130-size can L 0.3-1 mH not published) is >> the 50 us PWM period: ripple <= ~0.3 A p-p worst, extra copper loss < 0.02 W/motor. Heating follows average current, i.e. the same as DC at V_cap.
motor_rail.brush_wear: commutation arcing scales with the PEAK applied voltage, so 12.6 V PWM wears brushes somewhat faster than 6 V DC (not quantifiable from any datasheet); acceptable for a TT-class motor (EUR 6-13, spare bought). Speed and gearbox wear follow the average voltage, which the cap limits.
motor_rail.failure_mode: firmware fault at 100 % duty puts 12.6 V on the motors: Hiwonder 2.5 A stall each, 5 A/channel = MDD3A peak; FIT0450 5.9 A each -> MDD3A over-current shutdown. Mitigation: the cap lives in the lowest PWM write function; watchdog brakes (LL); boot with PWM pins low.
motor_rail.alt_two_packs: Option: motors on the owned Elegoo 2S box (7.4-8.4 V, no cap needed), Pi on the 3S pack -> removes all coupling, costs space/mass (measure the 2S box first).

protection.fuse: 7.5 A ATM mini-blade in an inline holder with 18 AWG leads, right after the battery XT30. Normal max 2.4 A continuous; 4-motor stall burst 7.7 A (< 1 s); a pack short delivers >> 20 A. If the BMS trips below 7.5 A the BMS is the real protection -> still fit the fuse (BMS failure, wiring short ahead of the BMS).
protection.switch: the CAD's MTS-102-class mini toggle is typically AC-rated only (~3 A at 250 VAC, DC not stated): inadequate for 6-7 A bursts. Use a >= 10 A DC-rated rocker/toggle (e.g. Pololu #1406 10 A rocker, check its DC rating) or a MOSFET pushbutton switch.

wire.buck->Pi header: 20 AWG pair or 2 x 22 AWG pairs

protection.bulk_cap: 470 uF / 25 V low-ESR electrolytic at the MDD3A VM input + 47-100 uF at the buck input (Pololu warns about LC input spikes on hot-plug; a 3S pack can ring towards 2 x 12.6 V)

low_voltage_cutoff_3S.filter: 2 s average, ignore dips < 0.5 s, 0.3 V hysteresis
low_voltage_cutoff_3S.measure: ESP32 ADC1 pin, 47k/10k divider (12.6 V -> 2.21 V), 100 nF, calibrate with the multimeter (REQ-SCOUT-013)
low_voltage_cutoff_3S.bms: UNKNOWN whether the blue pack has a BMS. With a BMS: its cutoff (2.5-3.0 V/cell) is the last line. Without (bare LiPo with a balance lead): the firmware cutoff is the ONLY protection -> add a 3S LiPo buzzer alarm (~EUR 3).

distribution_table.node: 5 V bus -> ESP32 VIN, encoders, HC-SR04

payload_retention.verdict: an unrestrained cup SLIDES at 2.9-4.9 m/s^2; the sim's active e-stop (5.9 m/s^2) and a full-duty start (3.6 m/s^2) exceed that -> the payload needs a retainer (4 standoffs as a fence or a hook-and-loop pad) and the firmware must cap |a| <= 1.5 m/s^2 except for a true e-stop

com_limits.rule: front-lift and rear-lift accel >= 3.0 m/s^2 on flat, front-lift >= 0.6 m/s^2 with the nose 7.2 deg up

stop.LD19_note: LD19 datasheet gives NO accuracy below 300 mm; the 15 cm stop zone is 222 mm from the LiDAR
stop.verdict: stop budget 83 mm from 0.3 m/s at 1.5 m/s^2 (175 ms latency) -> 37 mm (C1) / 22 mm (LD19, accuracy unspecified < 0.3 m) margin inside 15 cm. Watchdog must brake (MDD3A LL): coasting takes 49-64 mm and > 300 ms in the sim.

cpr_required_x4.position_for_nav2_10cm: any encoder > ~20 cpr (10 mm/count) suffices for position; Nav2 arrival error is dominated by slip and map/AMCL error, not quantisation
cpr_required_x4.verdict: ~1000 counts/rev (x4) for PID down to 0.05 m/s at 50 Hz; below that use edge timing (period measurement) or a 100 ms window

odometry.esp32_counting: use the PCNT peripheral (classic ESP32 has 8 units; 4 needed, x4 decoding with both channels), glitch filter ~1 us; edge rate <= 16 kHz/motor is trivial for PCNT, a GPIO-ISR design would cost ~4 x 16k = 64k interrupts/s -> don't

gyro.verdict: feasible ONLY with (1) bias re-estimated at every stop (ZUPT), (2) gyro scale factor calibrated to <= 1 % (datasheet tolerance 3 % alone gives 10.8 deg on a 4x90 deg square), (3) wheel yaw excluded from the EKF (sim: 184 deg/10 m wheel-only; 55 deg/10 m when the slip calibration is for the wrong floor)

imu_placement.cad_r1: GY-521 hangs 10 mm under the top plate at x = 0, y = 0, chip facing DOWN
issues: URDF imu_joint has rpy 0 0 0 and z 0.059 (v1); CAD chip faces down at z ~0.050 -> URDF needs rpy (pi, 0, 0) [or the driver must flip axes] and the CAD z; a sign error in yaw rate is a classic EKF divergence

Pi 5 board spans x = 2.5-87.5 mm on the top plate: the IMU sits under the Pi's rear edge -> temperature swings of a few C when the CPU load changes; at the datasheet-derived 0.32 dps/C worst coefficient 0.5 C of drift uses the whole bias budget -> ZUPT is mandatory, move IMU to x ~ -25 mm (still within 25 mm of the CoR), keep 10 mm air gap from the battery

LiDAR motor (C1 600 rpm = 10 Hz) and gear mesh vibration couple through the brass towers: set MPU DLPF to 44 Hz, sample >= 200 Hz on the ESP32, average to 50-100 Hz; nylon standoffs (already in CAD) help
magnetics irrelevant: MPU-6050 has no magnetometer; motor magnets do not affect a MEMS gyro
imu_placement.zupt: when |cmd_vel| = 0 and all encoder counts unchanged for 0.5 s: bias <- EMA(gyro, tau 5 s); publish with covariance; 40 % stationary duty in the mission profile gives frequent updates

ld19.size_mm: 38.6 x 38.6 x 33.5 body (54 x 46.3 x 34.8 with ears)
ld19.acc_note: +/-45 mm for 0.3-12 m; NO accuracy spec <= 300 mm (D)
ld19.uart: TX only, 230400 baud, 3.3 V, ZH1.5T-4P; PWM pin -> internal speed control
ld19.ros2: ldlidar_stl_ros2 (vendor repo, ROS 2 support community-maintained for Jazzy)

c1.uart: TX+RX 460800 baud 3.3 V, XH2.54-5P; USB adapter in kit

why: accuracy specified (+/-30 mm) from 0.05 m, so the 15 cm stop zone (222 mm from the LiDAR) is inside spec; LD19 has no accuracy spec below 300 mm
0.72 deg vs 1.0 deg: 2 beams per 5 cm cell out to 2.0 m (LD19 1.4 m)
official, maintained ROS 2 driver (sllidar_ros2) with a C1 launch file vs vendor/community LD19 driver
against: +63 g mass 15 cm above the floor (CoM +3.5 mm up; all stability margins still >= 3.5x, a6)
41.3 mm tall vs 34.8 mm, 55.6 mm square base; VCC window 4.8-5.2 V is tighter than LD19's 4.5-5.5 V -> feed it from the Pi USB (regulated) or straight from the D36V50F5, never via a long thin lead

payload_shadow.verdict: a seedling in the cup that grows > 5 mm above the 80 mm rim blinds a ~55 deg rear sector; either cap the payload envelope at 80 mm total height (REQ) or accept and filter a documented rear blind sector (laser angular-bounds filter) -- and never reverse blind

pitch_floor_hits.verdict: climbing the threshold pitches the robot 7.2 deg: the scan plane hits the floor 1.2 m away -> phantom obstacles / map corruption. Gate scans when |IMU pitch| > 1.5 deg (filter node) and set slam_toolbox minimum_travel to skip them.

cad.requirement: floor visible <= 150 mm ahead of the robot front (BRIEF: sees the floor >= 15 cm ahead)

camera.floor_requirement: floor visible <= 150 mm ahead of the front: CAD gives 109 mm -> PASS (41 mm margin)
camera.occlusion: lower FOV edge clears the camera mount by 9.4 mm and does not hit the HC-SR04 (it hangs under the top plate, below the lens line); check the real holder's front lip
camera.urdf: URDF r1 camera_joint has rpy 0 0 0 (v1); CAD pitches the camera 15 deg down -> camera_joint rpy must be (0, +0.2618, 0) and xyz from CAD lens centre (0.1105, 0, 0.0828) or detections are projected 15 deg off

fps.fps_320_estimate: ~4x fewer FLOPs -> 25-40 FPS inference-only (A: scaling, not measured)
fps.with_slam_nav2_load: expect 0.5-0.7x when 1-2 cores are busy with SLAM/Nav2 (A)
fps.verdict: REQ-SCOUT-010 (>= 10 FPS) FAILS at 640 px (7.8-15 FPS before other load) and PASSES at 320 px (est. 12-28 FPS under load). Use 320-416 px input, NCNN, 4 threads max 3.

ultrasonic.supply: 5 V only (datasheet 5 V DC, 15 mA); ECHO is a 5 V output -> divider to the ESP32 (not 5 V tolerant): 1 k (series) / 2 k (to GND) -> 3.33 V; TRIG accepts 3.3 V logic in practice (VIH not specified)
ultrasonic.range: 2-400 cm, 15 deg measuring angle (datasheet) -> blind < 2 cm, but reliable readings start ~3-5 cm (A)
ultrasonic.rate: 60 ms measurement cycle recommended (datasheet) -> 16 Hz max; at 0.3 m/s the robot moves 18 mm per ping
ultrasonic.coverage: beam centre z ~0.049 m (CAD, under the top plate); 15 deg cone covers z 0.029-0.069 m at 15 cm -> catches low obstacles the LiDAR (z 0.151 m) misses: shoes, pet bowls, door stops
ultrasonic.misses: soft fabric, thin chair legs at an angle, objects > 7.5 deg off-axis; never sole safety sensor

cable on floor.class: below scan: HC-SR04 / camera (also below sonar cone)
